metadata.title: DEVELOPMENT OF A CLINICAL PROGNOSTIC MODEL FOR UNSATISFACTORY FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES FOLLOWING TRANSOBTURATOR SLING SURGERY IN WOMEN WITH STRESS URINARY INCONTINENCE: A STUDY PROTOCOL
metadata.description: Transobturator midurethral sling surgery is an established surgical treatment for female stress urinary incontinence. However, postoperative continence, symptom improvement, and patient satisfaction are not uniform. A clinically useful prognostic model could support individualized counseling by estimating the probability of an unsatisfactory functional outcome before surgery.To describe a methodological framework for developing and validating a clinical prognostic model for unsatisfactory functional outcomes at 12 months following transobturator sling surgery in women with stress urinary incontinence.A prospective observational cohort study is proposed. Consecutive adult women undergoing transobturator sling surgery for demonstrable stress urinary incontinence or stress-predominant mixed urinary incontinence will be considered for inclusion. Preoperative demographic, clinical, and functional characteristics will be recorded using standardized assessments. The primary outcome will be patient-reported failure to achieve meaningful overall improvement at 12 months, defined prospectively using the Patient Global Impression of Improvement scale. Objective continence, persistent stress leakage, urgency symptoms, voiding dysfunction, and retreatment will be evaluated as secondary outcomes. A penalized logistic regression model will be developed using prespecified candidate predictors. Model performance will be assessed through discrimination, calibration, overall prediction error, and decision-analytic measures. Bootstrap resampling will be used for internal validation, followed by independent external validation.This manuscript presents a research protocol. No patient dataset has been analyzed, and no outcome frequencies, predictor coefficients, or model performance estimates are available.A transparently developed and independently validated prognostic model may improve preoperative counseling and the planning of postoperative follow-up. Its clinical usefulness must be demonstrated empirically before implementation.

metadata.title: The Third Case: Prompt-Governed Agency under a Consciousness Hypothesis
metadata.description:
English abstract

Can an artificial agent have subjective experience while lacking unrestricted authority to replace its governing task objective? This paper treats that possibility as a distinct design and evaluation problem, termed the third case. It separates phenomenal consciousness, goal-directed behavior, operational competence, temporal continuity, and decision authority. The hypothetical case, a functionally testable candidate, and the evidence concerning experience are different descriptions. The prompt-issuer is an explicit role that may itself be occupied by a potentially experiencing executor under upstream constraints. The framework preserves the project-specific composition B-Core = A-Core ⊕ Purple Box/Present. A-Core denotes a potentially stateful, learning, multi-model cognitive and executive system; Purple is an undisclosed candidate addition with intended history-dependent causal effects. ESSENTIAL is a protected specification of constraints and revision authority, logically associated with A-Core. A targeted comparison with IDA, LIDA, adjustable autonomy, and existing agent controls, at the access levels stated in section 2.4, locates the proposal within established work. The contribution is a project-specific evaluation contract for externally governed, internally continuous execution, rather than a demonstrated new consciousness mechanism. Three limited analytical observations concern goal delegation, policy differences masked by a shared guard, and the gap between an architectural effect and consciousness. The proposed studies distinguish causal relevance from practical benefit, score feasible completion and justified infeasibility separately, and control initialization, history transfer, order, and dependent observations. No empirical result or proof of phenomenal consciousness is claimed. Functional findings could remain valuable if the consciousness hypothesis is rejected; credible welfare concerns would require assessment that task success alone cannot resolve.

Magyar absztrakt

Lehet-e egy mesterséges ágensnek szubjektív átélése úgy, hogy közben nincs korlátlan jogköre irányadó feladatcéljának lecserélésére? A tanulmány ezt a lehetőséget önálló tervezési és értékelési problémaként kezeli, és harmadik esetnek nevezi. Elkülöníti a fenomenális tudatosságot, a célirányos viselkedést, a működési kompetenciát, az időbeli folytonosságot és a döntési jogkört. A hipotetikus eset, a funkcionálisan vizsgálható jelölt és az átélésre vonatkozó bizonyíték eltérő leírások. A promptot kiadó szereplő kifejezetten meghatározott szerepet tölt be, amelyet maga is betölthet egy esetleg átéléssel rendelkező, a hierarchia felsőbb szintjéről korlátozott végrehajtó. A keretrendszer megőrzi a projektre jellemző B-Core = A-Core ⊕ Purple Box/Present összetételt. Az A-Core egy potenciálisan állapotos, tanuló, több modellt használó kognitív és végrehajtó rendszert jelöl; a Purple egy nem közölt felépítésű kiegészítőjelölt, amelynek előzményfüggő oksági hatásokat szánnak. Az ESSENTIAL a korlátok és a módosítási jogkör védett specifikációja, amely logikailag az A-Core-hoz kapcsolódik. Az IDA-val, a LIDA-val, az állítható autonómiával és az ágensek meglévő irányítási megoldásaival végzett célzott összevetés a 2.4 szakaszban megadott hozzáférési szinteken helyezi el a javaslatot a korábbi munkák között. A hozzájárulás a külsőleg irányított, belső folytonosságú végrehajtás projektspecifikus értékelési szerződése, nem pedig egy bizonyított új tudatossági mechanizmus. Három korlátozott érvényű elemzési megfigyelés foglalkozik a célok delegálásával, a közös védelmi mechanizmus által elfedett döntésipolitika-különbségekkel, valamint az architekturális hatás és a tudatosság közötti különbséggel. A javasolt vizsgálatok megkülönböztetik az oksági relevanciát a gyakorlati haszontól, külön pontozzák a megvalósítható teljesítést és az indokolt megvalósíthatatlanságot, továbbá kontrollálják az inicializálást, az előtörténet átvitelét, a sorrendet és a függő megfigyeléseket. A tanulmány nem állít empirikus eredményt vagy a fenomenális tudatosság bizonyítását. A funkcionális eredmények akkor is értékesek maradhatnának, ha a tudatossági hipotézist elvetik; a hitelt érdemlő jólléti aggályok olyan értékelést igényelnének, amelyet a feladatsiker önmagában nem rendezhet.

metadata.title: Dataset for the paper "When LLM-Generated Refactorings Ripple: An Empirical Study of Repository Adoption Readiness"
metadata.description:
This dataset is associated with the paper titled “When LLM-Generated Refactorings Ripple: An Empirical Study of Repository Adoption Readiness”. The study examines whether LLM-generated refactorings of individual Java files are ready for adoption in the surrounding repository. Ten production files were selected from each of 15 open-source Java repositories (150 files) and refactored by five LLM configurations (Claude Opus 4.8, DeepSeek v4 Pro, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, GPT-5.5 and Qwen 3.6 Plus) under two generation conditions (a single prompt and a LangGraph-based multi-agent pipeline), yielding 1,500 generation attempts and 1,455 eligible refactoring candidates. Each candidate is assessed for contract/dependency risk, detected broken-caller evidence, a behavioural-equivalence indicator, targeted tests and adoption readiness. The data are stored in a Microsoft Excel file that consists of several worksheets. Below is a brief description of each worksheet.

No. Worksheet Description (as shown on the Zenodo record)
1 README The 'README' worksheet provides an overview of the study design, the LLM configurations, the risk indicators and the four adoption-readiness categories (Low-risk, Review-needed, High contract/dependency risk and Inconclusive), the analytical cohorts, the data flow between worksheets, missing-value handling, the statistical methods, data and code availability, and the limitations.
2 Paper_map The 'Paper_map' worksheet identifies the worksheet and cell range of every table, figure, cohort figure and research-question result reported in the paper, with a direct link to each location and notes on values that differ between the paper and the dataset.
3 Codebook The 'Codebook' worksheet defines the terms and analytical cohorts used in the paper and every column of the raw and processed worksheets, maps the logged field names to the paper terminology, and indicates which fields are used in the paper.
4 Study_Setup The 'Study_Setup' worksheet presents the subject systems (Table 1), the pipeline stages, the LLM configurations, the model invocation settings (Table 4), the analytical cohorts and the repository profiles of the 15 Java repositories.
5 Raw_Selected_Files The 'Raw_Selected_Files' worksheet contains the 150 selected production Java files (ten per repository) with their repository-exposure indicators, including LOC, PMD smell count, fan-in, fan-out, public and caller-used APIs, downstream callers and the dependency-risk score, with values unchanged.
6 Raw_Single_Prompt The 'Raw_Single_Prompt' worksheet contains the 750 single-prompt generation attempts (150 files × 5 LLMs) across 64 logged fields, with the logged values unchanged.
7 Raw_Multi_Agent The 'Raw_Multi_Agent' worksheet contains the 750 multi-agent generation attempts (150 files × 5 LLMs) across 64 logged fields, with the logged values unchanged.
8 Generation_Attempts The 'Generation_Attempts' worksheet contains the 1,500 generation attempts with eligibility, contract and overall risk, broken-caller evidence, the behavioural-equivalence indicator, risk-reason coverage, targeted-test outcome, adoption-readiness category and artifact availability. It is the source data for RQ2–RQ5.
9 RQ1_Exposure The 'RQ1_Exposure' worksheet presents Tables 5–7, which report the repository exposure of the 150 selected files by project and overall, the Kruskal–Wallis comparisons across projects with Holm-adjusted p-values, and the Spearman correlations among the exposure indicators, followed by the file-level source data.
10 RQ2_Risk_Indicators The 'RQ2_Risk_Indicators' worksheet presents Tables 8–10, which report the prevalence of High contract/dependency risk, detected broken-caller evidence and the behavioural-equivalence indicator among the 1,455 eligible candidates, the risk mechanisms among the 864 reason-covered candidates and the threshold sensitivity analysis, followed by the source data for Figure 3 and the candidate-level data.
11 RQ3_Comparisons The 'RQ3_Comparisons' worksheet presents Tables 11–14, which report the paired single-prompt versus multi-agent comparisons over 705 complete condition pairs (McNemar and Wilcoxon tests), the mechanism-level comparisons, and the model comparisons over complete five-model blocks (Cochran’s Q, Friedman and Holm-adjusted post-hoc tests), followed by the pair-level and block-level data.
12 RQ4_Adoption_Readiness The 'RQ4_Adoption_Readiness' worksheet presents Tables 15–17, which report the four adoption-readiness categories with Wilson confidence intervals, the coverage of each verification-evidence layer (including 395 test-eligible candidates and 65 conclusive test outcomes) and the categories per LLM, followed by the candidate-level evidence data.
13 RQ5_Associations The 'RQ5_Associations' worksheet presents Tables 18–19, which report file-level and candidate-level associations between source-file characteristics and the three outcomes (Spearman’s ρ and Cliff’s δ with Holm-adjusted p-values), the risk-mechanism overlap and edit-telemetry analyses, followed by the file-level and candidate-level data.
14 Raw_Data_Manifest The 'Raw_Data_Manifest' worksheet lists the original raw data files of the study (results exports, repository profiles, risk-reason, test and edit-telemetry records), with the number of records, primary identifiers, related research questions and availability status of each file.
15 Artifact_Manifest The 'Artifact_Manifest' worksheet records, for each of the 1,500 generation attempts, which artifacts are retained (raw response, candidate source, diff, profiles, verification report, compile and test logs). Candidate source artifacts are retained for 187 eligible candidates and complete artifact bundles for 166 eligible candidates.

metadata.title: PHOTO-CAT: Photometric Contamination Analyzer Tool
metadata.description:
PHOTO-CAT is a catalog-driven, mission-agnostic tool for quantifying stellar flux contamination in wide-field photometric observations. High-precision photometric missions are sensitive to flux from neighboring stars, which can bias light curves, dilute transit depths, and degrade photometric precision; PHOTO-CAT screens targets for that risk directly from an astrometric catalog, before an observation is planned.

The pipeline builds a three-dimensional Euclidean representation of the sky from a user-provided catalog and indexes it with a memory-optimized KDTree for rapid neighbor searches. A streaming, CSR-style storage format with compact internal identifiers keeps memory overhead low enough to process catalogs with tens to hundreds of millions of sources. Per-target contamination is then computed from angular separations, relative fluxes, and a configurable aperture model: a top-hat, or a circular Gaussian PSF that weights each neighbor by the fraction of its flux falling inside the aperture, out to an influence radius equal to the aperture radius plus the PSF extent.

Catalog flux can optionally be converted into another photometric band before contamination is computed, either by integrating a blackbody spectrum through the band's transmission curve, which works for any mission passband including filters pulled from the SVO Filter Profile Service, or by applying a published Gaia empirical colour transformation, for the photometric systems and colour ranges those relations are calibrated on. Official transmission curves for Gaia, TESS, CHEOPS, MAUVE and the six Ariel channels ship with the package.

Outputs include per-target contaminating flux, contamination ratios, target purity, the number of neighboring sources and their angular separations, written as JSON alongside reproducibility metadata recording the package version, the query configuration, the index manifest and the explicit scope of the model. The tool runs from a graphical configurator or from a command-line interface. Results are catalog-level screening estimates, meant to support target selection and field-geometry decisions ahead of observations rather than to correct measured photometry.

The method and its application to the Ariel Mission Candidate Sample are described in G. Galletta et al. (2026), "PHOTO-CAT - Photometric Contamination Analyzer Tool: A High-Performance Framework for Photometric Contamination Assessment"; this reference is updated with its DOI once the article is published. Although developed for the Mauve satellite, PHOTO-CAT is mission-agnostic and readily applicable to TESS, PLATO, Ariel and other wide-field surveys.

metadata.title: Entering and Leaving Childhood: Threshold Poetics in Sergei Aksakov  and Erkin A'zam
metadata.description: The paper compares two narratives that stand at opposite ends of childhood: Sergei Aksakov's  Childhood Years of Bagrov's Grandson  (1858), which tells how a child enters the world of perception, and  three novellas by the Uzbek writer Erkin A'zam (The Street of Little Devils,  Ice Cream  and  Farewell to  the Fairy Tale), which tell how a child leaves childhood behind. Using the anthropological concept of the  threshold (van Gennep, Turner), narratology and the typological method of comparative literature, the  paper argues that the two traditions mark the boundary of childhood differently. In Aksakov the threshold  is crossed through a widening of perception and the gradual accumulation of impressions; in Erkin A'zam  t is crossed through a moral event, the discovery of adult untruth and the need to choose. The contrast  illustrates  a  broader  tendency:  Russian  prose  places  the  meaning  of  childhood  in  the  growth  of  consciousness, while Uzbek prose places it in conduct and moral trial.

metadata.title: Energy in Extended Classical Mechanics (ECM): Mathematical Support — Part - 2
metadata.description: This paper provides the formal mathematical support for the Extended Classical Mechanics (ECM) framework introduced in Part 1. Building on the tripartite state progression of existence — the latent state, the phase state, and the manifest state — we derive explicit functional forms for the latent force limit F_latent = g(Δx) that satisfy the structural constraints of ECM: a bounded displacement domain within the pre-Planck interval (ℏℏₚ/360²) · (1/360) ≤ Δx ≤ (ℏₚ/360)·(359/360), asymptotic divergence as Δx → 0 while remaining finite at every discrete non-zero state, and consistency with the potential-gradient relation F_latent = −dPE_ECM,latent/dΔx. Two candidate forms are developed: (1) an inverse-power potential gradient exhibiting power-law hyper-stiffness, and (2) a phase-modulated exponential barrier incorporating 360-degree geometrical scaling. We evaluate the definite transition integrals of the energy-accounting scheme, demonstrating that transferred potential energy ΔPE_ECM between any two non-zero displacement endpoints is finite and maps directly onto kinetic energy ΔKE_ECM under the ECM positive-magnitude convention. The explicit velocity scaling of the emergent manifestation is derived, and the partition of the latent reservoir into residual effective potential energy (PE_ECM)^eff and transferred energy ΔPE_ECM is formalized. Four mathematical distinctions are preserved throughout: latent-state divergence versus finite states; the displacement interval versus the transition threshold ℏₚ/360; potential versus transferred energy at vanishing displacement; and phase velocity versus propagation velocity.

metadata.title: IBV GI-19 S1 alignments, phylogenies and metadata supporting global diversification analyses
metadata.description:
This dataset contains S1 sequence alignments, phylogenetic trees and associated metadata supporting the study “Global diversification and molecular evolution of the IBV GI-19 lineage reveal the emergence and predicted structural signatures of contemporary circulating clades”.

The deposited files include:

  • The S1 nucleotide alignment and global phylogenetic tree for 4,457 infectious bronchitis virus (IBV) sequences.
  • The GI-19 reference alignment and phylogenetic tree using H120 as the outgroup.
  • Sensitivity-analysis alignments and trees using YN and 4/91 as alternative outgroups, and H120 after exclusion of candidate recombinant sequences.
  • Metadata for the 4,457 sequences, including sequence identifiers, sampling dates, geographic origins, lineage assignments, GI-19 reference-group labels and within-GI-19 recombination-screening status.

The complete GI-19 dataset contains 1,951 ingroup sequences. Exclusion of 21 candidate recombinant sequences identified by RDP5 produced a sensitivity-analysis dataset of 1,930 ingroup sequences; outgroup sequences are additional to these counts. Clade A–I labels refer to assignments in the original reference phylogeny and are retained for descriptive comparisons across analyses.

Public sequence records were retrieved from NCBI Nucleotide on 23 September 2025. The deposited files document the datasets used for the analyses rather than a continuously updated collection.

metadata.title: MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS AND ORGANIZATIONAL EFFECTIVENESS IN NON-STATE EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS: AN EMPIRICAL ANALYSIS
metadata.description: The rapid expansion of non-state education requires management systems that combine regulatory compliance, instructional leadership, resource stewardship and public accountability. This study examines organizational development in Uzbekistan’s non-state educational sector through a descriptive secondary-data analysis, with general secondary education serving as the principal empirical case. Official statistics for the 2023/2024–2025/2026 academic years were analysed alongside the national education law, accreditation regulations and international research on school leadership and non-state provision. The number of non-state general education institutions rose from 293 to 551, while enrolment rose from 64,103 to 157,471 learners. Between 2024/2025 and 2025/2026 alone, institutions increased by 21.1% and enrolment by 40.5%. In 2025/2026, Tashkent city and Fergana region accounted for 48.3% of these institutions. The study distinguishes observable system expansion from organizational effectiveness, which cannot be established using counts of schools and learners alone. On this basis, a five-domain governance and effectiveness assessment matrix and a staged evidence-to-improvement cycle are proposed. The findings show where management capacities may be placed under pressure by expansion and geographic concentration, but do not demonstrate institution-level causal effects. The proposed framework is intended for subsequent school-based validation through records, staff and parent surveys, instructional observation and longitudinal outcomes.

Every page of the edition is anchored to its page of the master scan (file 91); each volume has a contents page and bookmarks to every part.

The integration and audit (S16). Every one of the 1,162 master pages of Nallino's three volumes is edited (1,131) or disposed (31); the two other editions are covered page by page; the 42,388 anchors of the corpus are unique. metadata.description: TinyWhisper is a fully integrated, open-source multi-mode short-wave transmitter for amateur radio applications, fabricated in 130-nm CMOS on a 2 mm × 2 mm die, using the IHP Open-PDK. It combines an analog IQ modulator front-end with a digital core featuring a RISC-V CPU, a 30-bit CORDIC-based sine/cosine generator, and a Delta-Sigma modulator, enabling multiple radio modulation schemes (including WSPR) with fine frequency resolution down to approximately 0.05 Hz. Beyond its primary use as a ham radio transmitter, TinyWhisper serves as a showcase of what is achievable with fully open-source EDA tools and open PDKs, covering the complete design flow from system design and RTL through tapeout, packaging, PCB design, and a 3D-printed enclosure. It is also suitable for ham radio courses, technical college and university courses, and regression testing of open-source toolchains.

Mother lineage  Microrobotic Sampling and Quantum Biosensing Co-Design at the Limit  Publication Abstract This monograph asks whether microrobotic samples collected across position, depth, and time can support causal discrimination within disease microenvironments rather than merely produce biomarker heatmaps. The scientific object is the complete chain linking tissue state, transport, sampling path, probe footprint, multimodal measurement, candidate causal graph, local intervention, and held-out outcome. Spatial proximity, predictive accuracy, and cross-modal agreement do not establish direction when position, batch, cell composition, measurement error, or common calibration can explain the same pattern. The framework treats causal tomography as an uncertainty-bearing inverse problem that may remain non-unique. Tumor, chronic-inflammation, and fibrotic microenvironments are evaluated as separate test platforms. The central falsifiable proposition is that a safe, local, reversible perturbation should distinguish at least some mechanisms that generate the same terminal phenotype. If intervention data do not separate the models, if conclusions are prior dominated, or if sampling changes the disease state, the result is downgraded to a descriptive atlas or an unresolved equivalence class.   Scientific Position and Hard Boundary A high-resolution map is not automatically a mechanism map. A microrobot can deplete analytes, redistribute fluid, compress matrix, alter local temperature, create adsorption memory, or preferentially reach some regions. Quantum sensing can improve selected measurements, but it can also add optical, thermal, magnetic, preparation, and readout costs. These effects enter the causal model as measured variables and uncertainty sources rather than disappearing behind the terms minimally invasive or quantum enhanced. Candidate Research Expression Cmicro = Iid Across Rintervention − Eequiv − Dsampling − Bprior  • Iid measures the identifiability of the declared causal parameters. • Across measures agreement across genuinely informative and independently referenced modalities. • Rintervention measures agreement between predicted and observed responses to a held-out local intervention. • Eequiv measures the remaining set of observationally or interventionally equivalent models. • Dsampling measures distortion caused by the sampling path, footprint, depletion, carryover, or tissue contact. • Bprior measures how strongly the conclusion is supplied by prior assumptions or regularization. Authorization, tissue safety, irreversible harm, missing raw evidence, broken sample identity, and failed independent references are hard vetoes. No favorable score can cancel them. An intervention-aware architecture for distinguishing mechanisms from spatial association

Main result

Mother lineage

Microrobotic Sampling and Quantum Biosensing Co-Design at the Limit

Publication Abstract

This monograph asks whether microrobotic samples collected across position, depth, and time can support causal discrimination within disease microenvironments rather than merely produce biomarker heatmaps. The scientific object is the complete chain linking tissue state, transport, sampling path, probe footprint, multimodal measurement, candidate causal graph, local intervention, and held-out outcome. Spatial proximity, predictive accuracy, and cross-modal agreement do not establish direction when position, batch, cell composition, measurement error, or common calibration can explain the same pattern.

The framework treats causal tomography as an uncertainty-bearing inverse problem that may remain non-unique. Tumor, chronic-inflammation, and fibrotic microenvironments are evaluated as separate test platforms. The central falsifiable proposition is that a safe, local, reversible perturbation should distinguish at least some mechanisms that generate the same terminal phenotype. If intervention data do not separate the models, if conclusions are prior dominated, or if sampling changes the disease state, the result is downgraded to a descriptive atlas or an unresolved equivalence class.

Scientific Position and Hard Boundary

A high-resolution map is not automatically a mechanism map. A microrobot can deplete analytes, redistribute fluid, compress matrix, alter local temperature, create adsorption memory, or preferentially reach some regions. Quantum sensing can improve selected measurements, but it can also add optical, thermal, magnetic, preparation, and readout costs. These effects enter the causal model as measured variables and uncertainty sources rather than disappearing behind the terms minimally invasive or quantum enhanced.

Candidate Research Expression

Cmicro = Iid Across Rintervention − Eequiv − Dsampling − Bprior

• Iid measures the identifiability of the declared causal parameters.
• Across measures agreement across genuinely informative and independently referenced modalities.
• Rintervention measures agreement between predicted and observed responses to a held-out local intervention.
• Eequiv measures the remaining set of observationally or interventionally equivalent models.
• Dsampling measures distortion caused by the sampling path, footprint, depletion, carryover, or tissue contact.
• Bprior measures how strongly the conclusion is supplied by prior assumptions or regularization.

Authorization, tissue safety, irreversible harm, missing raw evidence, broken sample identity, and failed independent references are hard vetoes. No favorable score can cancel them.

An independent assay then determines whether the system identified the mechanism, merely memorized position or batch, or changed the state it attempted to explain.

metadata.description:
This archive contains processed data, analysis code, computational settings and supporting outputs for a study integrating imidacloprid-associated candidate targets with colorectal cancer (CRC) transcriptomic features.

The materials include source accession inventories; original GEO preprocessing scripts, cached platform annotations and raw-input manifests; normalized expression matrices; differential-expression, weighted gene co-expression network and enrichment analyses; comparison of 113 machine-learning pipelines; Enet model results and SHAP analysis; fixed-Enet nested cross-validation and paired-dependence sensitivity analyses; individual-gene ROC evaluation in GSE44861; and focused molecular docking inputs, grid configurations, logs, poses, scores and redocking RMSD results. In the revised machine-learning analysis, GSE110224 and GSE23878 were processed separately without joint ComBat adjustment with Train. Docking used AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 with exhaustiveness 32 and a maximum of 10 output modes.

The main analysis begins from the supplied normalized gene-expression matrices and prepared docking structures. A separate module provides the six original raw-file preprocessing scripts; two were recovered verbatim from RStudio source caches. All six supplied preprocessing output matrices were byte-identical to the corresponding analytical inputs. Full raw preprocessing was not rerun during packaging. Public raw data remain available from GEO and RCSB PDB through the accession numbers documented in the archive. The README describes input snapshots, execution steps, software dependencies and the verification performed during packaging. Third-party data and code retain their source terms, as detailed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

Mother lineage  Microrobotic Sampling and Quantum Biosensing Co-Design at the Limit  Publication Abstract This monograph examines whether a microrobot can use an initial measurement to select a subsequent sampling location, time, volume, or sensing intensity while preserving the physiological state it claims to estimate. It treats the complete observation–action–state chain as the scientific object. Motion, signal amplitude, and controller accuracy are insufficient when sample identity, localization, disturbance, calibration, authorization, or uncertainty cannot be reconstructed. The architecture advances through phantoms, microfluidic challenge courses, organ-on-chip systems, authorized ex vivo tissue, and separately governed preclinical platforms. It makes no claim of present human deployment, diagnosis, treatment, dosing, or autonomous intervention. Its central falsifiable proposition is that, at matched disturbance, time, sample, and energy budgets, a bounded closed loop should provide more independently validated state information than fixed sampling. If the apparent gain is explained by additional measurements, hidden human correction, sample alteration, or untraceable calibration, the claim fails.   Scientific Position and Hard Boundary The book starts from a strict distinction: observing a biological system is itself an intervention. A microrobot can redistribute analytes, perturb tissue, create heat, apply force, alter local flow, or change the timing of later observations. Quantum sensing can add sensitivity in selected settings, but it can also impose optical, thermal, magnetic, preparation, and readout costs. These effects are measured rather than hidden behind the labels minimally invasive or quantum enhanced. Candidate Research Expression Uloop = ΔIstate Psafe Ptrace − λs Dsample − λm Dmeasure − λo Roff-target  • ΔIstate measures the reduction in uncertainty about the declared physiological state. • Psafe is the probability that actions remain inside the preregistered physical, biological, and authorization envelope. • Ptrace measures continuity of sample, location, time, device, sensor, calibration, model, and decision provenance. • Dsample and Dmeasure represent disturbance created by sampling and measurement. • Roff-target represents burden imposed on unintended tissue, samples, regions, or downstream decisions. Safety, authorization, irreversible harm, missing raw evidence, and invalid provenance remain hard vetoes. They cannot be cancelled by a favorable weighted score.   Five-Layer Research Architecture 01 State and Claim Contract  Define the physiological state, available actions, permitted use, disturbance limits, comparator, uncertainty, and conditions requiring abstention. 02 Transport Sampling and Interface Physics  Quantify flow, diffusion, wall drag, contact, adsorption, shear, heat, fields, capture, release, recovery, and off-target burden. 03 Quantum and Classical Measurement  Bind raw quantum observables and classical comparators to selectivity, calibration ancestry, uncertainty, drift, and measurement backaction. 04 Estimation Decision and Safe Control  Use explicit belief states, expected information gain, partial observability, safe exploration, human override, and tiered authorization. 05 Test Ladder Transfer and Successor Choice  Advance only through blinded testbeds, independent reproduction, fault injection, portability, creator-absent rebuild, and a real option to retire the system. Minimum Verifiable Prototype A blinded analyte gradient is embedded in an organ-on-chip testbed. Fixed sampling, expert-adjusted sampling, and a bounded autonomous closed loop receive matched time, energy, sample-volume, and disturbance budgets. The closed loop may choose the next location and measurement intensity only inside its registered safe action set. Independent assays reconstruct the hidden gradient and evaluate whether information gain remains after sample damage, localization error, sensor backaction, and extra sampling are accounted for.   Research Contributions • Treats sampling as a state-changing intervention rather than a neutral collection step. • Connects microrobotic navigation, quantum measurement, state estimation, and safe control within one falsifiable chain. • Requires quantum channels to compete against fit-for-purpose classical sensors after preparation, readout, energy, and backaction costs are counted. • Maps thirty physically and statistically distinct derivations to specific chapter, experiment, and Research Gate corridors. • Provides eighty-two chapters with five research pages per chapter: boundary, mechanism, minimum experiment, adversarial validation, and successor route. • Turns two hundred Research Gates into complete future-study cards containing baseline, evidence, competing explanation, stop condition, next path, and handoff packet. • Preserves negative results and allows fixed sampling, conventional assays, or human control to remain the stronger answer. What the Book Does Not Claim The monograph does not report a completed human trial or establish that autonomous in-body sampling is currently safe or clinically effective. Organ-on-chip and ex vivo results cannot substitute for human evidence. Quantum sensitivity does not automatically imply diagnostic utility. Any translational program requires independent biological, engineering, ethical, regulatory, clinical, and post-market validation. metadata.title: Daily Precipitation Dataset for Brazil (1980–2024) Based on Machine Learning with Improved Skill for Intense Rainfall Events
metadata.description:
This dataset provides daily precipitation records from 8,463 rain gauge stations across Brazil, covering 1 January 1980 to 31 December 2024. Derived from observations from the Brazilian National Water and Sanitation Agency (ANA) Hidroweb network, the dataset integrates quality-controlled observations with precipitation estimates generated using machine learning and spatial interpolation.

We reconstructed missing precipitation values using a Random Forest hurdle model, selected through a systematic comparison of eight candidate methods, including five supervised machine learning approaches and three spatial interpolation baselines. We evaluated model performance using cross-validation with contiguous gaps of 7, 15, and 30 days, followed by an independent confirmatory test. The selected model improved over inverse-distance weighting (IDW) for moderate-to-intense rainfall, reducing root mean square error (RMSE) by up to 9.9% for specific precipitation intensity classes.

The dataset is distributed as a compressed archive containing individual CSV files for the 8,463 stations, accompanied by a README and data dictionary. Each station file provides daily precipitation observations, Random Forest and IDW estimates, and variables identifying the origin and availability of precipitation values. Full-calendar reconstructions and historical-record reconstructions are provided separately, allowing different analytical applications while preserving the distinction between observed and estimated precipitation.

The dataset supports hydrological modeling, precipitation climatology, extreme rainfall analysis, flood-related studies, and assessments of hydroclimatic variability across Brazil. Its long temporal coverage and extensive station network provide a valuable observational resource for investigating precipitation patterns and hydrological extremes in a region characterized by substantial climatic and geographic diversity.

Temporal coverage: 1980–2024
Spatial coverage: Brazil (8,463 rain gauge stations)
Temporal resolution: Daily
Variable: Precipitation (mm day⁻¹)
Data format: CSV files distributed in a ZIP archive
Methods: Random Forest hurdle model and inverse-distance weighting (IDW)
Data source: Agência Nacional de Águas e Saneamento Básico (ANA), Hidroweb.

metadata.title: Visit-matched relative density (RD) 30 m rasters for forests of the conterminous United States from TreeMap 2023 and 2022, with a stress test against FIA plots
metadata.description:
Wall-to-wall relative density (RD) for forests of the conterminous United States at 30 m, built by giving each TreeMap pixel the RD of the FIA plot visit that TreeMap imputes to it (TreeMap 2023, primary; TreeMap 2022, stability check). RD follows the locked convention of Weiskittel et al.: additive metric Reineke SDI over live trees of at least 2.54 cm on forest conditions, per forested plot area, divided by the plot-level Bayesian (brms) maximum SDI, capped at 1.

The record also holds 1 km means for display, the Value-to-RD lookup tables that rebuild the 30 m rasters from the public TreeMap products, the aggregated tables of a stress test of the maps against 123,915 FIA plots (visit nearest 2022), and all code. Against FIA plots, 40.2 percent of TreeMap 2023 forest pixels sit at or above RD 0.60 against 42.2 percent of plots, and across 81 EPA Level III ecoregions the mapped share above 0.60 follows the plot share (r = 0.83). Because TreeMap imputes FIA plots, this agreement is a consistency check and not independent validation, and agreement at individual pixels is weak (r = 0.25 at true plot locations in Maine). The tables also report summary statistics of the Vibrant Planet 2024 ForestDensity layer for comparison; that layer is not redistributed here.

No FIA plot coordinates, true or public, appear in any file. A graphical abstract (00_rd-visit-treemap2023_graphical_abstract.png) is the lead visual.
